title: George Sayles and six-string banjo players
summary: Allen and Ridgley discuss George Sayles on guitar and viola, and six-string banjoists such as Johnny St. Cyr, Louis Keppard and John Marrero.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What did George Sayles play? What instruments? Banger, a guitar.
He did play banger? He played guitar. And he played, not violin, what's it called? The viola.
The viola.
Yeah. He was a, him and I was back east. I was a violin player. And him and George Orton, I played together. Viola and violin.
Did he play a four-string banjo ever? Or do you remember?
No, he played guitar.
Guitar.
Yeah.
George Sayles. I just wondered, because some of those guys, you know, had trouble changing and some of them liked the six-string banjo.
I see.
You remember Bud Scott and Johnny Saint-Cyr both played those six string bandages? Six string.
Well all the other played with us played six string. We never did have a first string. Who were they?
Who were some of the men that played six string?
Johnny Saint-Cyr.
Yeah, he played, and who else?
And Louis Kevick. Yeah. And who else played with me a while?
What about John Marrero?
Yeah, he had six string. He was good.
I like the sound of a six string. You know you can get those low notes and go upon and everything.

Well a six string. Full range. I think it sounds, you know, you didn't make it look like pure like that. So then the fellas can't get over a six string bandage would be good but they can get over a four. But they hadn't got the sound like the six.
